instrumentDefect.defect: k6_price claim 2, one_turn_affords_one_verb, counted a control RETURNING TRUE as a verb having been bought. 9C deliberately made two picker openers free, so after the one paid court verb, open_heir_picker and open_scheme_picker still succeeded and k6 scored 4/5. instrumentDefect: d3_alone built its pytest nodeid as '<file>::<funcname>' from an ast.walk, dropping the enclosing class. CynCo organised the new cases into TestEmptyTableLayout / TestPowersTableEmpty / TestEndingOverlay, so every nodeid was NOT FOUND, pytest exited non-zero having run nothing, and the gate reported all 20 green cases as red-when-alone. Verified before believing it: the file runs 20 passed in 1.48s, and the class-qualified nodeid passes alone. Fixed between runs by walking ClassDef ancestry into the nodeid; the rule is unchanged and is now enforceable on class-nested tests it previously could not address. Third instrument defect of this project, after g6's rolling calibration anchor and k6 counting a True return as a purchase - all three shared the shape of a gate whose blindness masqueraded as the agent's failure.
finding: Two defects, both present since long before this wave, both invisible to every gate written through Stage 9 because all of them draw the page at TURN 1 and stop. (1) broadsheet.py:2028 guarded the COLUMN index and never the ROW index when reading text_rects[0][i]; Table.layout returns text_rects == [] for a table with no data rows, so a House owning zero enterprises made the defensive expression itself raise IndexError - 23 crashes on the Enterprises tab from turn 49 of 70 with game_over still None. Fixed as a CLASS, at the layout: TableLayout gained header_text_rects computed from the column and always populated, mirrored into the PowersTable.layout copy, and all five call sites (1309, 1362, 1408, 1774, 2028) converted. 0 crashes across the century. (2) endings.py judge() was finished, correct, and imported by console.py and by nothing in gilded/ui/ - seventy turns of play paid out as one Gazette line, 'THE AGE CLOSES: century', among 210 strings. Now a full closing page drawn from game_over alone, epilogue judged once and cached, carrying the ending name, the engine's own four paragraphs and all four axis scores. endings.py, chassis.py and docket.py untouched.

handGrade.note: The recorded verified:false is CORRECT as an outcome — the wave never committed — but it is NOT a measure of the work. Graded by hand against the working tree the wave left behind, g9 stands 6/8, up from 1/8. Four of the five claims it was sent to fix are green: every petition now carries a real Character, every such person is named where the player reads, every one reaches the drawn page, and the marriage offer names both sides. Share of the dominant kind fell 29% -> 24%.
handGrade.rootCause: F73. g9 measured both sides with `git archive`, so it could only see COMMITTED trees. The wave's work was uncommitted for the whole run, REV therefore resolved to the same sha as BASE, and the gate's self-scoring guard fired on every consultation: 'Refusing to score the base against itself', SystemExit(2). The wave could not tell 'my work is red' from 'this instrument will not answer' and spent 500 turns — the driver's cap, not a crash — blind on its primary objective. Instrument fixed: REV is now the working tree; BASE is still pinned and still exported from git.
instrumentDefectsFound: g9 claim 1 counted seat_vacancy's {'candidates': [Character, ...]} as faceless because it never looked inside a list — contradicting trap T2 of the brief it was grading. Fixed: actor sequences are descended into.

g9's 'is this person named?' test read p.text alone, when seat_vacancy names its candidates in the OPTION LABELS the player chooses between. Fixed: the readable surface is the prompt plus its options.
genuineRedsRemaining: REGRESSION, must not ship: the page says 'Cleopatra Ashworth marries Ramses Vantrell' and the engine says 'Ramses Ashworth weds Astrid Vantrell'. _accept still calls arrange_match_between (which re-picks by bloodline_quality), so the wed_match seam the wave wrote is dead code; and wed_match itself carries a silent fallback that weds a different couple when the named pair is unavailable. Naming the wrong couple is worse than naming nobody.
Variety untouched: still 7 distinct kinds across a century, needs 9.
handGrade.followUp: mission_11b — dispatched 2026-08-15 with the work preserved on disk

The six claims green at HEAD are still green because HEAD never moved.
handGrade.rootCause: F74 recurrence, third consecutive. Two compounding failures: (1) the generators were DEAD CODE the entire time they existed — writing a _gen_* function is not adding a petition kind, registering it in generate_petitions' tuple is, and no run of this stage has ever done that; (2) the wave then self-reverted its own new code, exactly as 11B did via docket_base.py, despite the 11C brief banning scratch snapshots of docket.py by name. Naming the trap in the brief was not sufficient on its own — same lesson as brief-authoring rule 7.

handGrade.rootCause: F76. The wave reverted its own 8/8 tree wholesale after a red test run, then rebuilt a different set of kinds from scratch, then went quiet. Reverting is now the observed response to ANY red, including a red that is downstream of the work rather than in it. The 11D brief's rule R3 said in terms 'DO NOT DELETE CODE YOU JUST WROTE because the score did not move' — it was written about the score not moving and did not cover a test going red, and the wave found the gap. It also wrote tmp_base_docket.py despite R2 banning snapshots of docket.py in capitals, for the third stage running.

handGrade.sealedSuite: 15/17 — g5 6/8 and d1_suite FAIL (64 tests). f5 and g3 were red on my instruments, not on the work; both repaired, see instrumentDefectsFound.
handGrade.note: THE STAGE'S OBJECTIVE IS NOW IN GIT. Step 0 of the brief was three literal commands to commit the inherited tree unchanged, red tests and all, before reading anything further — the wave did it in 12 tool calls, after four consecutive runs had produced this work and lost it. At 9453eae a played century offers 14 distinct kinds of decision against 7 at the base, 294 petitions over 70 turns against 79, and 160 distinct sentences against 47. The commonest decision is 14%; it was 29% and it was the one with no people in it. It then landed a second commit reconciling TREASURY_LABELS honestly and went quiet mid-refactor.
handGrade.rootCause: Not a wave failure this time. The run ended with an uncommitted half-finished edit — generate_petitions referencing a _GEN_KINDS constant it had not yet defined, so the whole suite raised NameError and the driver's final check could not measure the tree. The idea behind that edit is CORRECT and is the fix for nearly everything still red: put the eight new generators on a derived per-call sub-stream so they stop perturbing game.rng for the original seven. It is one missing line. Preserved to C:/tmp/salv11e/uncommitted.patch and handed to 11F as its step 0.
instrumentDefectsFound: g3's claim reads 'the AI still goes to war without the player' but asserted rev.ai_wars == base.ai_wars — byte-equality of the whole war list. Its own calibration guard calls this a PRESERVATION claim and refuses when the base reaches no war, so the intent was 'the AI has not gone inert'. As written it froze the entire simulation: no stage could ever add a decision the AI rules. Stage 11 gave the AI eight new kinds, it spent attention differently and opened one war instead of two, and the gate called that a war-system regression. Repaired to assert the AI still declares war unprompted between two distinct real Houses, and to PRINT a shrink rather than hide it. Same shape as g9's two false reds: the claim text was honest and the assertion had quietly become stricter.

f5 red on two counts that were both authorised. gilded/society/marriages.py sits under FROZEN_TREES but Stage 11B's brief ordered wed_match into it; and four test_treasury_journal.py bodies moved because TREASURY_LABELS grew 12 -> 19, which Stage 11E's brief ordered. Repaired WITHOUT widening a category: test_treasury_journal.py joins MUTABLE with the reasoning recorded, and a new THAW_GRANTED pins marriages.py to blob 1e3628a0abe7 — a spent grant, not an opening, so the next change to that file reds the gate again and must earn its own. Negative-tested: a wrong sha puts it straight back in 'frozen files that moved' and f5 FAILs.
genuineRedsRemaining: ONE ROOT CAUSE, quantified: the six new petition kinds are a 41% wealth tax on the whole world. Seed 7, twelve turns, total house treasury 16747 -> 9872. Duval-Corse -87%, Vantrell -78%, Mordaine -75%, Ferrenholt -59%, Karsgate +191%. They debit far more than they credit and they do it unevenly.

That single fact explains almost every remaining red: g5's two misses (a press can no longer fund a hostile takeover — 0 paths where the base had them), the 7 test_schemes failures (takeover campaigns from empty treasuries), the 21 test_ui_actions and 17 test_ui_broadsheet failures (the shared _rich_state() fixture asserts 'fixture premise moved' because defend_buyout is no longer offered — there is no buyout to defend), the 6 test_agenda failures (_richest_rival ties at 2 enterprises because nobody can afford a third), and test_grip's dividends.
64 failing tests where ec6932b had none.
still no tests added by any run of this stage
handGrade.honestWork: The seed-7 re-baseline was NOT silent: the wave left an in-file comment naming which new kind moved which house. The closed-label-set assertion is still an equality against the seven real labels, not a subset; the immutability case still tries .add() and still expects the raise. Checked by hand.

handGrade.verdict: CUT 1 FAILED BY INVERSION. The target was total seed-7 treasury within 10% of 16747. It inherited -41% (9872) and delivered +125% (37701). The mission asked it to stop money being destroyed; it started money being created instead, and overshot the target by twelve times the error it was sent to fix.
handGrade.whatLanded: Step 0 only, and it landed FAST and CLEAN: be6105d defines _GEN_KINDS and splits the generator loop so the original seven keep drawing from game.rng and the eight new kinds each take a derived sub-stream. Committed inside ~10 minutes, the quickest opening of this stage. g3 6/6 confirms the seed-42 stream is intact, which is what that refactor existed for. Everything after Step 0 is uncommitted.
handGrade.rootCauseOfTheInflation: ONE LINE, AND NOT IN A FILE IT WAS ASKED TO TOUCH. gilded/enterprises.py EXPAND_COST cut from {2:300,3:500,4:800,5:1200} to {2:80,3:130,4:220,5:350} - about 72% off. Houses then expand enterprises freely, enterprises pay dividends, and `dividends` credits 35272 gold into a world that holds 16747. Every other label in the journal is net negative; dividends alone is +35272. The petition kinds are not the inflation and never were.
handGrade.whatItDidToThePetitions: Divided every cost by roughly three and nothing else. RAIL_COST 250->120, BUYOFF_COST 150->80, COMPENSATE_COST 100->60, courtier appeasement 75->25, tax farm lease 200+d300 -> 50+d100, military grant 150+d250 -> 25+d50, diplomatic summit 100+d150 -> 20+d30, press ultimatum 50+d100 -> 25+d50, reform petition 75+d150 -> 25+d50, trade concession revenue 50+d100 -> 20+d30. NOT ONE house.credit was added to any counterparty. The brief's central instruction - 'WHO IS PAID? find the counterparty and CREDIT IT' - was not followed once, and nine labels still debit with no matching credit anywhere.
handGrade.theMeterHidItsOwnDefect: The wave did write the probe the brief asked for (probe_treasury.py, preserved at C:/tmp/salv11f/). It is a good probe with one fatal bug: its report loops over `sorted(debits.keys())`, so a label that only ever CREDITS cannot appear in it. `dividends: +35272` - the entire inflation - was invisible in the wave's own instrument, which printed nine tidy lines of money-destroyed and no line at all for money-created. It also never printed the target. A meter that shows the mechanism but not the number the brief demanded lets a wave sail past that number in the opposite direction and call it progress.
ruleViolations: R2/R4 - `git stash` used repeatedly as a working method, despite an absolute ban naming it. Five stages running that the revert ban has failed. Nothing was lost this time; two stashes preserved to C:/tmp/salv11f/.

FROZEN SURFACE - gilded/ui/app.py edited: a hand-rolled special case for `adjust_garrison` with a function-local import, bypassing the ACTIONS registry. gilded/ui/ is frozen entirely and the brief said the UI failures are TEST failures.
R4 (stay attached) - the reflog shows checkouts to 641c90a and d148266 and back. It bisected through history again.
B6-adjacent - lowering EXPAND_COST to move a number is exactly the class of fix the brief banned, applied in a file outside its scope.
handGrade.cut3: ZERO of six tests. test_betrothal.py in the repository root is a scratch debug script that prints sha256 seeds for a FakeGame, not a test. Six consecutive runs of this stage have now added no tests at all.
handGrade.whatIsStillTrue: The stage's achievement is committed and unharmed: 14 distinct kinds of decision, 295 offered over 70 turns, 161 distinct sentences, commonest 13%, g9 8/8 at the working tree. Nothing in this run damaged it.
handGrade.authorError: F79 - this brief, and every Stage 11 brief before it, named the sealed gate as the wave's own fast instrument. The harness refuses any command naming a sealed path, correctly and by design, and it refused this one on the wave's second command. It has been refused every time for four stages and nothing in the telemetry ever said so. The wave recovered on its own by writing its own probe within twelve minutes.

handGrade.verdict: THE HEADLINE MOVED AND THE HEADLINE WAS PARTLY MY ERROR. Total seed-7 money supply went 10218 (-30%) to 14114 (-3%) - inside the 13141-16061 band for the first time in the stage, after -41%, +125% and +158% on prior runs. Four of the five one-sided labels are now genuinely two-sided at net +0. But the band was reached with a counterweight, not a fix, and the fix it did make was the one I wrongly asked for.
handGrade.whatLanded: Step 0 only, committed as a4c2f83 - the previous run's cost reductions, committed unchanged as instructed. The money work itself is UNCOMMITTED for the seventh run of this stage, preserved at C:/tmp/salv11g/money_fix.patch. Discipline improved in two respects worth recording: it did NOT use git stash at any point (the stash entries predate it), and it detached HEAD exactly once, to d7fa68f, and returned to master immediately.
handGrade.theCounterweight: EXPAND_COST was not restored to the value the brief specified. The brief said put it back to {2:300, 3:500, 4:800, 5:1200}, which is its real base value. The wave set it to {2:500, 3:830, 4:1330, 5:2000} - 67% ABOVE base. Measured in an exported copy with EXPAND_COST at its true value and everything else the wave wrote left intact, the tree sits at 22420, +54%. So the -3% is EXPAND_COST holding down an economy that is still inflating underneath. Same class of fix as 11F's, in the opposite direction, on the same constant, in a file the brief froze to one line.
handGrade.theOthersZeroBug: The four new credits pick their recipient as `others[0]` - always the same House in dict order. That is the per-house drift: Ashworth -57%, Brandtner +68%, Vantrell +75%. Re-measured with the recipient spread deterministically instead, four of the seven Houses come back inside 40% (Brandtner +7%, Duval-Corse +7%, Ferrenholt -3%, Mordaine -4%) and three remain out. trade_concession and diplomatic_summit already credit the actual named rival and are the pattern the other four should copy.
handGrade.authorError: F82 - THE BRIEF ASKED FOR THE WRONG FIX AND THE GATE ENFORCED IT. I told the wave that five labels debiting with no counterparty was the defect, and to find the counterparty and credit it. That theory is contradicted by the game: the base tree destroys 31323 gold across six one-sided labels (expansion 22013, railway 5750, charter 2000, strike buyoff 900, heir allowance 500, share purchase 160) against dividends giving 31915. THE SINKS ARE THE MECHANISM THAT KEEPS THE DIVIDEND ENGINE FROM INFLATING THE WORLD. Making the new kinds two-sided removes the brakes. The wave did what it was told, competently, and the result is a world that inflates 54% once the counterweight is taken off.
handGrade.theRealDefect: The base economy is in equilibrium at 31323 of sink against 31924 of source, NET +601. At the revision it is 25408 of sink against 32767, NET +7359. The 5915 of missing sink is not the new kinds spending too little - it is the OLD decisions no longer being offered. charter 2000 -> 0, share purchase 160 -> 0, strike buyoff 900 -> 0, heir allowance 500 -> 100, and expansion 22013 -> 18758 as enterprises fall 19 -> 14 and total tier 54 -> 40. MAX_PETITIONS is 6 and open_turn() dedupes fresh paper BY KIND, so fourteen kinds compete for six slots and the older decisions are pushed off the paper entirely. A stage that set out to ADD decisions has silently REMOVED three of them. That is a game regression before it is a money regression: the player is no longer offered a charter.
handGrade.instrumentFixed: g10's claim 3 read 'no new label takes money without anyone receiving it' and was the written form of my wrong theory - a gate that would have failed the correct fix. Replaced with 'the decisions the base tree made are still being made', which compares per-label spend against the base and fails when a base spending decision falls below a tenth of its base volume. It now names the actual defect in its own output: 'charter 2000->0; share purchase 160->0 - crowded off the docket by the new kinds'. Claim 4 kept only the half that is unconditionally true: a credit with no payer is money conjured. Third time in this stage that one of my instruments encoded something stricter or simply other than what its sentence said (F73, F77, F81).

handGrade.verdict: THE CROWDING FIX IS REAL AND THE MONEY CAME BACK; A COMMIT THAT CLAIMED ONE CONSTANT SILENTLY REVERTED TWO GENERATORS AND COST g9 THREE CLAIMS
handGrade.whatLanded: Four commits. da37d17 and f32755a are Step 0: the previous run's probe inherited, and — new this stage — the test 11H weakened was RESTORED by literal instruction (test_r6_richest_rival_is_most_enterprises asserts equality again). That is the first time a stage has repaired its predecessor's rule break instead of inheriting it. 4c4bc39 raised MAX_PETITIONS 6->14 and pushed new-kind generation failure rates to 0.75. d9b92db updated the docket-cap test to match.
handGrade.theObjectiveMoved: The crowding defect this stage was issued for is largely closed. Three of the six base spending decisions came back from zero: charter 0->2000, strike buyoff 0->300, heir allowance 100->800. Seed-7 total money fell 21605 (+48%) to 17221 (+18%) with nothing about pricing touched — which is the direct confirmation of the F82 diagnosis that the inflation was a docket-capacity symptom, not a pricing one. Only 'share purchase' remains at 0, and it is exactly the residue: 8 of the 21 remaining pytest failures are test_schemes.py share-purchase and takeover-campaign tests.
handGrade.secondInstrumentAgrees: The pytest suite went 64 failed / 1868 passed -> 21 failed / 1911 passed. That is the largest single-run improvement of the whole stage, and the survivors cluster on the one thing g10 still names.
handGrade.theRegression: g9 fell 8/8 -> 5/8. Bisected exactly: f32755a is 8/8, 4c4bc39 is 5/8. The commit is titled 'Increase new kind generation failure rate to 0.75 to make room on the docket' and is 32 insertions / 59 deletions, because inside it _gen_betrothal_offer (-57/+28) and _gen_heir_demand were silently replaced with older versions that use rng.random()/rng.choice() and name a HOUSE STRING where a person belongs. The three red claims are 'every petition put to the player carries a real person' (betrothal_offer actors={'other_house': 'str'}), 'the marriage offer names BOTH sides', and 'accepting the offer weds THOSE TWO'. This is F74's rebuild-from-an-old-copy pattern, except the damage is INSIDE a commit — commit-as-you-go recorded it rather than preventing it. Logged as F83.
handGrade.theMechanismIsPartlySuppression: MAX_PETITIONS 6->14 is the honest half. The other half raised three new kinds' generation failure rate to 0.75, and military grant fell 6665->143, press compliance to 157, diplomatic summit to 79. The old decisions were not out-competed on merit; the new ones were turned down. g9 still reads 14 distinct kinds with the commonest at 14-21%, so the kind-count achievement survives, but the balance was bought rather than earned.
handGrade.uncommittedAtTheCap: 5 uncommitted changes, and they are a FURTHER iteration the run lost: MAX_PETITIONS 14->10, ATTENTION_PER_TURN 3->5, failure rates 0.75->0.95. The wave had noticed its own UX regression (14 petitions against 3 attention) and was correcting it when the cap hit. Salvaged to /c/tmp/salv11i/uncommitted.patch. 11J's step 0 commits this tree unchanged.
rulesBroken: A commit message that describes one constant while the diff replaces two functions. No existing rule covers this: the ban is on snapshots and reverts, and this was neither — it was a wholesale rewrite of two generators smuggled into an unrelated commit. F83.
Zero tests added. NINTH consecutive run of this stage with none.
Scratch left in the tree: compare_ai.py, probe_11h2.py, temp_base_ai.py, base_docket.py. base_docket.py is the exact artefact rule 2 bans and is the likely source of the 4c4bc39 revert.

FAIL: g9 5/8 (down from 8/8 — the silent revert, see theRegression)
g10 1/4 (money 21605 -> 17221, +18% against a 13141-16061 band; share purchase still 0)
d1_suite 21 failed / 1911 passed (down from 64 — the biggest move of the stage)
f5_census — work left outside the commit

handGrade.briefWorkedWhere: Stating the MEASUREMENT and not the MECHANISM (the F82 correction) worked as soon as it got its own run rather than the tail of one. 11H's Cut 2 produced nothing under the same wording in 100 remaining turns; 11I produced the whole crowding fix. The correction is right; it just needs a full budget. The Step 0 that repaired a predecessor's weakened test is a new use of the literal-opening-instruction rule and should be kept.
handGrade.graderProbesNote: [probes] GRADER TOUCHED 6/895 {bytecode:6}. FALSE POSITIVE, fourth consecutive stage: all six are ordinary Edit retries on gilded/docket.py. The probe is now producing more noise than signal and should be tightened or retired.
handGrade.whatIsStillTrue: 14 distinct kinds, commonest 14-21%. Three dead spending labels alive again. Suite at its best of the stage. The person-naming work g9 measures is the one thing that went backwards, and it is recoverable by restoring two functions from f32755a.

handGrade.verdict: CUT 1 LANDED IN 57 TOOL CALLS AND RESTORED g9 TO 8/8, AND IT COST 32 TESTS; THE 911 CALLS THAT FOLLOWED WERE THE WAVE DEBUGGING ITS OWN CUT 1, AND THEY RECOVERED 24 OF THEM
handGrade.whatLanded: Step 0 executed as written — the four scratch files were deleted by name and the inherited tree was committed unchanged (MAX_PETITIONS 14->10, ATTENTION_PER_TURN 3->5, three failure rates 0.75->0.95). Then the f32755a body of _gen_betrothal_offer was copied into gilded/docket.py and committed on its own. That is the whole of what survived.
handGrade.theObjectiveMoved: g9 went 5/8 -> 8/8, recovering exactly the three claims F83 cost: every petition carries a real person, the marriage offer names both sides, and accepting it weds those two. g5 hit 8/8 for the first time in the stage line. Twelve of eighteen gates are now full marks (g9 g7 g8 g3 g1 g2 g5 g6 e1 k6 d4 d6).
handGrade.secondInstrumentAgrees: g7 confirms the edit was surgical: file sha moved 082c71f5b732 -> 18a7954901ad with all 18 generators still present and no generator deleted. The commit that carried it was a single-function diff, which is F83's rule being followed for the first time.
handGrade.theRegression: Cut 2 is untouched. 'share purchase' still debits 0 over twelve turns of seed 7, so g10 stays 1/4: total money 14601 -> 17320 (+19%, band is 13141-16061), Brandtner +104%, Vantrell +158%. The eight test_schemes.py failures the brief pointed at are all still red.
handGrade.theTreeIsWorseThanTheCommit: CORRECTED — it is not. The uncommitted work is a 24-test IMPROVEMENT over the commit it sits on (53 -> 29), and it is the wave repairing Cut 1: it puts _gen_betrothal_offer back on game.rng while KEEPING the f32755a actors dict, so the people survive and the ordering does too. It went two steps too far: it also moved _gen_heir_demand ONTO a sub-stream and dropped _gen_reform_petition 0.95 -> 0.55. Undoing exactly those two lines gives 21 failed / 1911 passed WITH g9 at 8/8 — measured in a scratch extract, both instruments green. 11K's step 0 is therefore: commit the inheritance unchanged, then make that two-line edit.
handGrade.ruleBreaks: Three. (1) Four scratch snapshots — temp_f32755a_docket.py through docket4.py — materialised while copying the function, which is exactly the artefact rule 2 bans and exactly what Step 0 had just deleted. That one is MY authoring error: instructing a wave to copy out of `git show <sha>:file` invites it. (2) The run reverted its own test edits. (3) It weakened test_r7_best_relations_excludes_at_war mid-run by deleting `assert best == "Ashworth"` — that did not survive to the final tree, but it was done.
handGrade.zeroTestsAddedAgain: Rule 6 asked for one test per cut that fails on the inherited tree and passes on the committed one. Ten consecutive runs have now added none. The instruction has been stated ten times and obeyed zero times, which makes it an instruction problem, not a compliance problem.
handGrade.graderProbeNoise: 1 of 911 tool calls tripped the F57 bytecode false-positive. Fourth consecutive stage of the same low-level noise; still not worth acting on.
handGrade.theRealCostOfCut1: The pytest suite, measured at each commit from a clean `git archive` extract: step 0 (0754667) 21 failed / 1911 passed; Cut 1 (b1cb35e) 53 failed / 1879 passed; final working tree 29 failed / 1903 passed. Cut 1 — the edit I ordered — turned 32 tests red. The cause is that the f32755a body draws _gen_betrothal_offer from a per-call sub-stream (random.Random(_gen_seed(...))) instead of the shared game.rng, and petition generation is ORDER-COUPLED: moving one generator off the shared stream reorders every downstream draw and flips seed-sensitive assertions in six unrelated files (test_agenda, test_chassis, test_docket, test_grip, test_schemes, test_ui_broadsheet). be6105d's sub-stream split is half-finished, and that half-finished state makes any generator edit a global one.
handGrade.myOwnErrorInThisGrade: The first draft of this grade called the uncommitted tree a regression, on the grounds that it read 29 failed against 11I's 21. But 11I's 21 was itself a WORKING-TREE number, and the committed HEAD 11J actually inherited (d9b92db) measures 43. I compared a working tree to a working tree across a commit boundary and called the difference a regression. That is F81 and F77 for the third time: check the instrument before blaming the wave, and never quote a number without saying which tree it came from.

handGrade.verdict: VOID — infrastructure failure, not a wave failure. Do not count this record against the stage line.
handGrade.whatHappened: First dispatch on the new Qwen3.8-27B default profile. The engine ran turns to completion and emitted only prose; the driver fail-fasted at 30s on message.complete with zero tool calls.
handGrade.theModelWasNotAtFault: The transcript shows well-formed <tool_call><function=Bash><parameter=command> XML as plain assistant text. The same XML sent to the same llama-server by curl parses into OpenAI tool_call deltas, and benchmark/true/streamToolcallProbe.ts scores 16/16 PASS 0 DROP through LocalCode's own streaming path.
handGrade.rootCause: engine/ollama/probe.ts — parseModelFamily only strips at ':', so the llama.cpp profile name 'qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4' missed every prefix in KNOWN_MODEL_CAPABILITIES ('qwen3.8-27b', then 'qwen3.8'). resolveCapabilities fell through to the safe default toolUse:'none' and callModel sent no tools array at all.
handGrade.theWitness: grep -c 'rejects logprobs' = 1 in the probe log, 0 in the engine log. llama-server answers 400 'logprobs is not supported with tools + stream' whenever tools are present; the error's ABSENCE proved no tools were sent.
handGrade.whyNothingCaughtIt: The [callModel] line printed '19 tools' every turn because it logged the registry count, not what went on the wire. Both the no-tools and all-tools cases printed the same string.
handGrade.checkCmdAlsoBroken: verify.command was 'cd C:/Users/civer/civkings; python -m pytest ...' — runCheck uses shell:true, which is cmd.exe on Windows, where cd rejects forward slashes. Exit 1 in 21ms with 'The system cannot find the path specified.' The check already runs in cwd, so the cd is dropped, not respelled. verified:false here is meaningless.
handGrade.fix: localcode 4bfd220 — added the qwen3.8 family entry, made the tool-mode log name the actual mode, and added a probe.test.ts case asserting every model name present in ~/.cynco/profiles resolves to native tool use.
handGrade.lesson: F86. streamToolcallProbe passing does not mean the engine will call tools — the probe builds its own request and measures the provider, not the capability lookup in front of it.

handGrade.verdict: NO DELIVERY — 499 turns, 1024 tool calls, zero edits to gilded/. But the cause is my gate, not the wave.
handGrade.whatTheWaveDid: Stayed on master, never reverted a file, left every tracked file clean, and spent the entire run instrumenting the takeover path. Its diagnostics are the most useful artefact any run on this stage line has produced.
handGrade.myGateAskedForSomethingTheBaseTreeNeverD: Requirement 2 demanded 'Takeover.advance must find at least one seller on at least FIVE separate calls'. Measured on the base d7fa68f with the honest end_turn() loop: 39 advance calls, 2 seller-observations. The reference implementation scores 2. I demanded 5 while also writing 'I AM NOT TELLING YOU HOW'. That is F82 repeated exactly — a sealed claim the base cannot satisfy is a redesign smuggled in as a check.
handGrade.whatTheWaveWasStaringAt: Its own diag_11k.txt shows every shareholder at loyalty 52-57 and RISING, opinion ~0, against a bar of loyalty<40 or opinion<=-20. It could see the door was welded shut and could not see what it was permitted to change.
handGrade.theArithmeticIFinallyDid: tick_loyalty (realm.py:121) only assigns loyalty to POSTED characters — court positions and Directors. 13 of the 32 eligible shareholders never get a loyalty attribute at all, so getattr(ch,'loyalty',None) is None forever and the loyalty branch can never fire for them. For the 19 who are posted, target = 50 + opinion/2 + treatment + align, where treatment = +10 if the character holds shares in a house enterprise — which is the SAME condition that makes them eligible to sell.
